blocks.text: 1. Top-K Selection
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447579557-409903824.png
Late Interaction Models closed with a pointer to this next topic. Top-K Selection closes the loop on the entire re-ranking pipeline by covering how many final results actually get passed forward.
It decides the exact number of re-ranked chunks that continue on to the language model.
2. The Last Decision Before The Model
In the two stage pipeline covered in Why Re-Ranking, retrieval found candidates and re-ranking ordered them carefully.
Top-K selection decides where that ordered list gets cut off.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Stage","Role"],"rows":[["Retrieval and re-ranking","Find and order candidate chunks"],["Top-K selection","Decides exactly how many to keep"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Choosing K, Revisited
The same tension behind choosing K in KNN reappears here, now applied after re-ranking instead of retrieval.
A small K keeps only the most confident results; a larger K keeps more, less certain ones.
4. Context Window As A Hard Ceiling

blocks.alt: Context Window As A Hard Ceiling
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447579557-356726070.png
As with the context window considerations covered in Parent Document Retrieval, the model's available context sets an absolute limit on K.
No amount of tuning can exceed that hard ceiling.
5. Quality Dropoff After Re-Ranking
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447580044-375621358.png
Re-ranking produces a sharp quality gap between the top few results and everything below them.
Results far down the re-ranked list often add little value to the final answer.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: After careful re-ranking, the relevance score often drops off sharply after the first handful of results, meaning results ranked tenth or beyond rarely add meaningful value.

blocks.text: 6. Too Small K Truncates Useful Context

blocks.alt: Too Small K Truncates Useful Context
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447580046-344337629.png
A K set too low can drop a relevant chunk that ranked just outside the cutoff.
This is especially risky for questions that need several supporting facts at once.
7. Too Large K Dilutes And Costs Tokens

blocks.alt: Too Large K Dilutes And Costs Tokens
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447580046-92053912.png
As with the risk of over expansion covered in Query Expansion, too many included chunks can dilute the model's focus.
Every extra chunk also costs real tokens and processing time to include.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Including twenty chunks when only three carry the actual answer forces the model to sift through irrelevant text, slowing it down and increasing the token cost of every single request.

blocks.text: 8. Dynamic K Selection Strategies
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447580047-369232663.png
Instead of a fixed K, some systems stop including results once the re-rank score drops below a threshold.
This adapts K per query rather than applying one fixed number everywhere.

blocks.content: {"headers":["K selection strategy","Behavior"],"rows":[["Fixed K","Always returns the same number of results"],["Dynamic threshold based K","Returns however many results clear a score cutoff"]]}

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing How To Set K For A Given Pipeline

blocks.alt: Recognizing How To Set K For A Given Pipeline
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447580047-181316782.png
Simple, single fact questions need only a small K.
Questions needing several supporting facts benefit from a larger K or a dynamic threshold instead.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates both fixed K and dynamic threshold based selection over re-ranked results.

code.content:
reranked_results = [
    {"id": "c1", "score": 0.94},
    {"id": "c2", "score": 0.89},
    {"id": "c3", "score": 0.85},
    {"id": "c4", "score": 0.41},
    {"id": "c5", "score": 0.33},
]

def fixed_top_k(results, k):
    # a fixed cutoff at position k
    return results[:k]

def dynamic_threshold_selection(results, threshold=0.6):
    # keeps results whose score clears a threshold
    return [r for r in results if r["score"] >= threshold]

fixed_selection = fixed_top_k(reranked_results, k=3)
print(f"Fixed K=3 selection:")
for r in fixed_selection:
    print(f"  {r}")

dynamic_selection = dynamic_threshold_selection(reranked_results)
print(f"\nDynamic threshold selection at 0.6:")
for r in dynamic_selection:
    print(f"  {r}")

print(f"\nNotice the sharp score dropoff after c3,")
print("which the dynamic threshold detects automatically.")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the dynamic threshold stopping right at the sharp score dropoff after c3, while a fixed K would have needed manual tuning to find that same cutoff.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Setting K without considering the model's available context window as a hard ceiling.
Using a K so small that it truncates supporting facts a multi part question actually needs.
Using a K so large that it dilutes the model's focus and wastes tokens on irrelevant results.
Applying a fixed K everywhere instead of considering a dynamic, score based threshold.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Top-K selection decides the exact number of re-ranked chunks that continue on to the language model.
It is the final decision after retrieval finds candidates and re-ranking orders them carefully.
The same choosing K tension from KNN reappears here, now applied after re-ranking.
The model's available context window sets an absolute limit that no tuning can exceed.
Re-ranking often produces a sharp quality dropoff between the top few results and everything below.
Too small a K can truncate relevant chunks that ranked just outside the cutoff.
Too large a K dilutes the model's focus and costs real tokens and processing time.
Dynamic threshold based selection adapts K per query instead of using one fixed number everywhere.
